study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized functional connectome abnormalities obtained using two normative model unveil neurophysiological subtypes of obsessive compulsive disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: A single-site clinical cohort from the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, comprising 99 patients with OCD and 104 healthy controls.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: we recruited a total of 99 patients with OCD and 104 healthy controls (HCs) matched for demographic characteristics... recruitment from outpatient services within the Department of Psychiatry at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University.

answer.SINGLE-SITE: normative training and performance evaluation (10-fold cross-validation) for the FCS model (HCs); clinical application for identifying OCD subtypes and clinical characterization (OCD patients)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The healthy control group (N=104) was used to train and validate the normative model. The OCD patient group (N=99) was used to derive individualized deviations (Z-scores) for subsequent subtype identification via clustering.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Subsequently, for each brain region, a Gaussian process regression model was trained to estimate the normative range of FCS values... within HCs. This model was then applied to each patient... We employed a data-driven k-means clustering algorithm to investigate potential subtypes within OCD. In this approach, individualized FCS abnormalities served as the clustering feature

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The study describes using 104 healthy controls for the normative model development and performance evaluation (10-fold cross-validation). Although the title mentions 'two normative model', the methods describe a single framework based on functional connectivity strength (FCS) using Gaussian process regression, applied across brain regions.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.reason: The paper explicitly states N=104 for HCs in Table 1 and Section 2.1. The 10-fold cross-validation was used for performance check, and the model was trained on HCs to provide the normative range for patient assessment. The mention of 'two' in the title is likely a typo for 'the' or refers to the two subtypes identified, as the methods only describe one normative modeling approach for FCS.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The healthy control group used for the normative model had a mean age of 23.14 years with a standard deviation of 5.64. No median or range values were reported for the HC group.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The HC group consisted of 51 males (49.04%) and 53 females (50.96%).
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.reason: Male count (51) and percentage (49.04%) are explicitly stated in Table 1 for HCs (N=104). Female count (53) and percentage (50.96%) were calculated by subtracting male values from the total N. Calculation: 104 - 51 = 53; 53 / 104 * 100 = 50.9615...% (rounded to 2 decimal places as per the paper's precision).
